stage_b_reviewed_content.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal S$ and $G:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal S$ be morphisms of categories fibred in sets over $\mathcal C$. Their $2$-fibre product exists in the $2$-category of categories fibred in sets over $\mathcal C$. Explicitly, its objects are quadruples $(U,x,y,\alpha)$ with $U\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$, $x\in\mathcal X_U$, $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, and $\alpha:F(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(y)$ in $\mathcal S_U$. Its morphisms are pairs $(a,b)$ over the same base arrow $U\to U'$ satisfying $G(b)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ F(a)$. This again defines a category fibred in sets over $\mathcal C$ and, with its projections, has the stated universal property.
